builder_plan.scenario: A product assistant retrieves plausible documents but gives unsupported answers.
builder_plan.change: Change one retrieval or ranking step while keeping the document snapshot fixed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retrieval pipeline with identical questions and answer model.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Supported answers, retrieval misses, correct abstentions, index cost, and response latency.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DuQUAD: A Dual-View Framework with Quality-Aware Evidence Pruning for Multi-Document Question Answering
summary: The method replaces standard RAG context packing and common Lost-in-the-Middle mitigations such as reordering, reranking, or generic multi-agent reasoning with a dual-view local/global agent design plus quality-aware pruning. It costs added orchestration and inference overhead versus a single-pass RAG pipeline, though the paper claims lower cost than prior multi-agent frameworks. It can fail when relevance or quality scoring is inaccurate, when pruning removes useful evidence, or when the extra local/global passes do not repay their latency and implementation complexity on a given workload.
rationale: The framework targets a production-relevant RAG failure mode and reports quality gains, but its value depends on whether the added dual-agent and pruning pipeline beats simpler retrieval and reranking under the reader's latency and budget constraints.
technique: Dual-view multi-document QA with evidence pruning

claims.statement: The method replaces standard RAG context packing and common Lost-in-the-Middle mitigations such as reordering, reranking, or generic multi-agent reasoning with a dual-view local/global agent design plus quality-aware pruning. It costs added orchestration and inference overhead versus a single-pass RAG pipeline, though the paper claims lower cost than prior multi-agent frameworks. It can fail when relevance or quality scoring is inaccurate, when pruning removes useful evidence, or when the extra local/global passes do not repay their latency and implementation complexity on a given workload.
Improves accuracy by 3.0% on average over the strongest baseline and gold evidence recall by 9.4%, while reducing computational cost relative to existing multi-agent frameworks.
